item.title: One-Sided Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators on Variable Lebesgue Spaces Beyond Log-H\"older Continuity
item.description: arXiv:2611.03835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the boundedness of the right-sided Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over the real line. Motivated by the $K_0$ condition for the classical Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator, we introduce a directional condition $K_0^+$ adapted to the geometry of the one-sided maximal operator. We characterize $K_0^+$ in terms of the uniform boundedness of a family of one-sided averaging operators and prove that it is a necessary condition for the boundedness of $M^+$ on $L^{p(\cdot)}(\mathbb{R})$. We also establish one-sided analogues of the modular and reverse H\"older estimates associated with the classical $K_0$ condition. These estimates constitute the main local ingredients in the proof of boundedness of $M^+$ under the combined assumptions $K_0^+$ and $N_\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Lucas A. Vallejos

item.title: Bounds for Orthogonal Expansion Coefficients via Weighted Primitives
item.description: arXiv:2611.04067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For trigonometric and polynomial orthogonal expansions, we present coefficient bounds with an explicit numerator determined by the total variation of the function and the largest cumulative signed area of the weighted basis element. This area, denoted by $M_n$, is the sharp constant in the corresponding weighted integral estimate. We calculate or bound $M_n$ for several classical systems, thereby obtaining quantitative inequalities beyond an asymptotic statement of coefficient decay. Integration between consecutive zeros gives a geometric interpretation of the estimate. The comparison includes Chebyshev polynomials of the first three kinds, Legendre, Jacobi, Gegenbauer, and ordinary Laguerre polynomials, with normalization and boundary conditions stated explicitly. Classical estimates and their elementary consequences are organized as Fourier analysis in inequalities. In the controlled distortion application, ideal curves have selected coefficients absent, and restrictions on the variation, corridor width, and number of extrema of admissible departures give explicit guarantees for those coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Sluchak

item.title: Poisson area and non-tangential maximal functions on manifolds with ends and applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.04177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M=\mathbb R^m\sharp(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb S^{m-n})$, where $m>n\geq3$. The full-cone Poisson area and non-tangential maximal functions fail to be of weak type $(p,p)$ for $1<p<2$. Let $K$ be the compact part joining the two ends and put $\rho(x)=1+d(x,K)$. For fixed small $c>0$, we restrict the horizontal distance from the vertex to $c\rho(x)$ and retain every positive time. The resulting maximal function is of weak type $(1,1)$ and bounded on $L^p$ for $1<p\leq\infty$. The corresponding area function uses the full spatial and time gradient. It satisfies a Fefferman--Stein distribution inequality. Its $L^p$ norm is equivalent to that of $f$ for $1<p\leq2$. This area function defines a global Hardy space. We prove its $\Delta$-atomic description, its injective embedding into $L^1$, its characterization by the restricted maximal function, and its real interpolation identity with $L^2$. Direct estimates for spectral-band kernels then give a Mihlin multiplier theorem from this Hardy space to $L^1$. Interpolation and duality give $L^p$ boundedness for every $1<p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Peng Chen, Ji Li, Lixin Yan

item.title: A sharp Mittag-Leffler bound for series with separated exponents
item.description: arXiv:2611.04540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\eta\geq 0$ and $\delta>0$, and let $(r_j)_{j\geq 0}$ be a sequence of real numbers satisfying $\eta \leq r_0 < r_1 < r_2 < \cdots$ and $r_{j+1}-r_j \geq \delta$ for every $j\geq 0$. We prove that, for $\delta\leq 1$ and every $x>0$, \[ \sum_{j=0}^\infty \frac{x^{r_j}}{\G(1+r_j)} \leq \sum_{j=0}^\infty \frac{x^{\eta+j\delta}}{\G(1+\eta+j\delta)} = x^\eta E_{\delta,1+\eta}(x^\delta), \] where $E_{\delta,1+\eta}$ denotes the two-parameter Mittag-Leffler function. Moreover, equality holds for some $x>0$ if and only if $r_j = \eta + j\delta$ for every $j$. The proof combines a finite compression argument for unimodal functions with a shift inequality for the Mittag-Leffler function. The upper bound $\delta \leq 1$ is sharp, since counterexamples exist for every $1 < \delta < 2$.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Molteni

item.title: Bilinear Kor\'anyi spherical maximal function on the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2611.04549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the bilinear Kor\'anyi spherical means on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n,$ and derive $L^{p_1}(\mathbb{H}^n) \times L^{p_2}(\mathbb{H}^n) \to L^{p}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ estimates for the associated bilinear Kor\'anyi spherical maximal function on $\mathbb{H}^n.$ We also address multilinear extensions of our results.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Ghosh, Rajesh K. Singh

item.title: Sampling Density for Multi-window STFT Phase Retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2611.04877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study phase retrieval for multi-window short-time Fourier transforms with windows given by complex linear combinations of the first two normalized Hermite functions. Assume that the family of window coefficient vectors does phase retrieval in $\bbC^2$. We prove that the multi-window magnitude samples uniquely determine every signal in $L^2(\bbR)$ up to a global phase whenever the sampling set is separated with lower Beurling density greater than $2$, or is a translated lattice with density at least $2$. Moreover, we show that the sampling density is the best possible, which improves a result in [P.~Grohs, L.~Liehr, and M.~Rathmair. Multi-window {STFT} phase retrieval: lattice uniqueness, J. Funct. Anal., 288(3): Paper No. 110733, 23, 2025].
item.dc:creator: Wenchang Sun, Mengxuan Zhou

item.title: Arithmetic product theorems on self-similar sets of uniqueness and homogeneous Moran sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.04956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Varj\'u and Yu have given a complete description of non-singleton self-similar sets of uniqueness on the real line $\mathbb R$. In this paper, we first prove an arithmetic product theorem for self-similar $U$-sets $E:$ if $F\subset\mathbb R$ is compact, then $F\cdot E$ is an $M_0$-set if and only if $F$ is uncountable. We next show that this conclusion remains valid for bounded integer-based homogeneous Moran sets. As an application, for every $s\in(0,1]$, there exists a bounded integer-based homogeneous Moran set of uniqueness $K$ such that $\dim_H K=s$ and the self-product $K\cdot K$ is an $M_0$-set. In sharp contrast, for every $s\in[0,1/2]$ we can construct an unbounded integer-based homogeneous Moran $U$-set $E$ with $\dim_H E=s$ such that both $E$ and $E\cdot E$ are $U$-sets, and $1/2$ is the optimal threshold for $U$-sets to be closed under the arithmetic self-product. Moreover, we show that if $E\subset[0,1]$ is a compact set whose self-product $E\cdot E$ is contained in an $H$-set, then $\underline\dim_B E\le1/2$.
item.dc:creator: Yan-Song Fu, Xu-Guang Wang, Meng Zhu

item.title: Stein's generalized spherical maximal operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.05154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This survey concerns Stein's analytic family of generalized spherical means and the associated maximal operator. We review Stein's original theorem, the sharp necessary conditions for boundedness, and the complete theory for radial functions. We then explain the connection between positive results and local smoothing estimates for the half-wave propagator and, more generally, for Fourier integral operators. This point of view yields the sharp two-dimensional result through the work of Guth, H. Wang, and R. Zhang and, when combined with the recent local smoothing theorems, an improved higher-dimensional range. As a byproduct, the maximal operator associated with the first radial derivative of spherical means is bounded on $L^p(\R^4)$ for $2<p<3$, a case left open in recent work of Kwa\'snicki. We keep track of the relation between the local smoothing exponents and the resulting maximal estimates, and identify the region that remains open.
item.dc:creator: Luz Roncal

item.title: Limit cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.04245v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we consider cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane. Our first result shows that there exists a limit cycle of singular algebraic foliations such that the limit cycle cannot be realized in any affine chart, that is, it fails to appear in any affine plane via the usual dehomogenization. On the other hand, under an appropriate convexity assumption, we verify that a cycle becomes fully visible, lying entirely in some affine chart. We then analyze the accumulation behavior of limit cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane. Last we prove that algebraic foliations of degree at most two on the real projective plane have only finitely many limit cycles, and the maximum number of limit cycle is zero, one and at least six for algebraic foliations of degree zero, one and two on the real projective plane, respectively. This result extends Bamon's finiteness theorem for quadratic affine vector fields in [Publ. Math. IH\'ES, (64)1986, pp. 111--142].
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Gan, Hongjin He, Dongmei Xiao

item.title: Sharp decay of the spherical averages of the Fourier transform of open sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.04426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, the spherical average $E_\Omega(R)=\int_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}|\widehat{\mathbb{1}_\Omega}(R\omega)|^2d\omega$ is never $O(R^{-a})$ with $a>d+1$, and for smooth boundaries it is $O(R^{-d-1})$, as it is for the ball, whether or not the boundary is curved. In 2003, Brandolini, Hofmann and Iosevich extended this to every convex domain and to every domain with $C^{1,\frac{1}{2}}$ boundary, and this regularity condition has not been improved since. How much regularity does the decay $R^{-d-1}$ require? We show that among H\"older classes the answer is $C^{1,\frac{1}{4}}$. Every bounded domain with $C^{1,\frac{1}{4}}$ boundary satisfies $E_\Omega(R)\leq C_\Omega R^{-d-1}$, while for every $0<s<\frac{1}{4}$ any smooth domain can be altered near a single boundary point to produce a $C^{1,s}$ domain for which this bound fails along a sequence of radii. More generally, when the boundary has fractional Sobolev regularity $W^{1+s,p}$, we determine the optimal decay exponent under a Dini condition on the normal, and in a large range of $s$ and $p$ without it. The upper bounds follow from $L^2$ estimates for nondegenerate oscillatory integral operators whose phases are distances between points of two graphs with Dini or fractional Sobolev gradients, and hence barely better than $C^1$. These are far too rough for the integrations by parts techniques from the smooth theory. We replace derivatives by finite differences adapted to the phase, a device that we expect to be useful in a variety of related problems.
item.dc:creator: A. Iosevich, A. Merlo, M. Mourgoglou

item.title: An oscillation result for slightly perturbed trigonometric series
item.description: arXiv:2611.04738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish that any nontrivial anharmonic Fourier series with exponents quadratically close to the positive integers changes sign on each interval of length 2$\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Alain Haraux (LJLL)

item.title: Matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces:characterizations, duality and interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04810v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $0<p<\infty$, $0<q,r\le\infty$, and $W$ be a matrix $\mathcal A_p$ weight on ${\mathbb R}^n$. We introduce the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces $Z^{p,q,r}_\alpha(W)$ and tent spaces $T^{p,q,r}_\alpha(W)$ on the upper half-space and establish their characterizations using reducing operators. We then characterize homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces in terms of the corresponding $Z$-spaces and tent spaces, respectively, using Schwartz kernels satisfying Tauberian and finite moment conditions. Furthermore, we establish duality for the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces and obtain real and complex interpolation results for these spaces and the associated homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces.
item.dc:creator: Tengfei Bai, Pengfei Guo, Jingshi Xu

item.title: Quasiconformal distortion of the lower dimension and applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.05118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the distortion of the lower dimension and lower spectrum of sets under quasiconformal mappings. As an application, we verify weighted Hardy--Sobolev inequalities in Euclidean domains arising as quasiconformal images of domains with sufficiently regular boundaries. The regularity in question is phrased in terms of estimates for either the Assouad or the lower dimension of the complement. We also provide dilatation-dependent classification results for certain planar open sets.
item.dc:creator: Efstathios Konstantinos Chrontsios Garitsis, Jeremy T. Tyson

item.title: On a property of plane curves
item.description: arXiv:0905.1308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\gamma:[0,1]\to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a continuous curve with $\gamma(0)=(0,0)$ and $\gamma(1)=(1,1)$. We prove that if $\gamma(t)\in(0,1)^2$ for all $t\in(0,1)$, then for each $n\in \mathbb{N}$ there exist points $A_1,\dots,A_n$ on $\gamma$ such that, with $A_0=(0,0)$ and $A_{n+1}=(1,1)$, the horizontal increments $\pi_1(\overrightarrow{A_iA_{i+1}})$ and the vertical increments $\pi_2(\overrightarrow{A_iA_{i+1}})$, $0\le i\le n$, are positive and coincide up to order. More generally, the same conclusion holds as soon as $\gamma$ contains an arc that joins two points of the diagonal segment, lies on one side of the diagonal, and satisfies a mild one-sided boundary condition. This covers, for instance, the graph of every continuous function $f$ with $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=1$, with no restriction on the range of $f$. In all cases the rearrangement can be taken to be a cyclic shift by one place of a block of consecutive increments. The main tool is a version of the mountain climbers' theorem in which one function is piecewise monotone and the other is an arbitrary continuous function. As an application, any two non-atomic probability measures on $[0,1]$ satisfying a mild condition admit, for each $n$, a partition of $[0,1]$ into $n+1$ consecutive intervals whose two lists of measures are rearrangements of each other.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, On a property of plane curves, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 361 (2010), 332--337
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Attainable forms of lower spectra
item.description: arXiv:2603.03174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varphi\colon(0,1)\to[0,d]$. We prove there exists a set $F\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ whose lower spectrum $\operatorname{dim}^{\theta}_{\mathrm{L}} F$ satisfies $(1-\theta)\operatorname{dim}^{\theta}_{\mathrm{L}} F = \varphi(\theta)$ for all $\theta\in(0,1)$ if and only if for all $\lambda,\theta\in(0,1)$, \begin{equation*} \varphi(\theta) \leq \varphi(\lambda\theta) - \theta \varphi(\lambda) \leq (1-\theta) d. \end{equation*} We also obtain a similar classification result for $\underline{\operatorname{dim}}^{\theta}_{\mathrm{L}} F$. In contrast to the case for Assouad spectra, it is insufficient to consider homogeneous (or uniform) sets. Instead, we follow the approach introduced by Orgov\'anyi--Rutar in arXiv:2510.07013 and proceed via a more general classification result for appropriate two-scale branching functions.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Banaji, Haipeng Chen, Alex Rutar, Wen Wang

item.title: A $Tb$ type theorem for suppressed kernels
item.description: arXiv:2606.26401v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, a non-homogeneous $Tb$ type theorem for arbitrary dimensional Calder\'on-Zygmund singular integral operators is proved. This is an extension of an analogous non-homogeneous $Tb$ theorem for the Cauchy transform, in the planar setting, due to Nazarov, Treil and Volberg. The novelties of the present work are the change of dimension and the fact that the operators to which the theorem applies are not necessarily antisymmetric. The techniques used in the proof include, among others, suppressed kernels, decompositions in $L^2(\mu)$, where $\mu$ is a Radon measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and a probabilistic argument resulting from taking averages of the operators involved.
item.dc:creator: Marina Fern\`andez-Vilaseca

item.title: Sparse domination modulo polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.09771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a sparse domination theory that captures both local polynomial approximation and cancellation of the input below the scale of each sparse cube. Its coefficients are percentiles of localized smooth maximal functions of the input minus its local polynomial approximation, combining features of mean-oscillation sparse bounds and of the cancellative sparse bounds of Conde-Alonso, Lorist and Rey. Using wavelet representations, we characterize the Calder\'on-Zygmund operators whose derivatives admit these bounds by explicit polynomial testing conditions. In the homogeneous setting, the same conditions characterize weighted Hardy-Sobolev inequalities with linear dependence on the $A_\infty$ characteristic. This quantitative dependence detects the transition from BMO to $L^\infty$ testing conditions that Lerner found for pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials, a distinction that qualitative weighted estimates cannot recover. In the inhomogeneous setting, we prove corresponding weighted inequalities and show that they are strictly weaker than pointwise sparse domination from the second derivative order onward. Consequences include Hardy-Sobolev estimates below the Banach range, sharp weighted Sobolev inequalities, and pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Di Plinio

item.title: Compactness and essential norms for two-weight fractional Riesz transforms on curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a compact two-weight $T1$ theorem for the $\alpha$-fractional Riesz vector, $0\leq\alpha<n$, when one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $\Gamma$. The measures may have common point masses. Under the global boundedness assumptions, we give a two-sided estimate for the essential norm in terms of Muckenhoupt and testing constants computed after restricting both measures to small cubes. Compactness is equivalent to the uniform vanishing of these local bounds as the cube side length tends to zero. The smooth truncations have a unique weak operator limit and converge in operator norm in the compact case. For arclength measure and distance power weights, we determine the compactness ranges for Green gradients on bounded tubes and for Newtonian gradients and Biot--Savart fields on the whole space. The whole-space operators in these ranges are compact but are not Hilbert--Schmidt. When $\alpha=n-1$ and both measures have positive continuous arclength densities $a,b$ on the same closed curve, we obtain the exact essential norm $\pi c_{n-1,n}\max_\Gamma\sqrt{ab}$.
item.dc:creator: Ji Li, Chun-Yen Shen, Chaojie Wen, Brett D. Wick, Liangchuan Wu

item.title: Another Application of the Alternating Map: Time-and-Band Limiting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01839v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use Castillo's dual formulation of classicality for the alternating map to reduce polynomial time-and-band limiting to two scalar problems. The reconstruction preserves polynomial cutoffs, multipliers and concentration forms. It recovers the symmetric Dunkl constructions of Castro and Gr\"unbaum and applies to continuous and discrete inputs. Scalar recurrences avoid moment factorizations; positive integrals and residual bounds control the accuracy of the concentration values.
item.dc:creator: L. Tertuliano da Silva

item.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
item.description: arXiv:2610.12434v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study whether global asymptotic stability (GAS) of the origin is decidable for homogeneous polynomial vector fields with rational coefficients. Our main technical contribution is showing that, for such vector fields of odd degree $d \geq 3$ in every sufficiently large dimension $n$, the problem of deciding GAS of the origin is many-one complete for the class of recursively enumerable sets (and hence undecidable). Using the tools we have built up, we also improve on some recent work by proving a similar result for Lyapunov stability instead of GAS. The proof of our main contribution splits naturally into two parts: - In the first part we give, for every fixed dimension $n$ and odd degree $2k+1$, a computable map which sends a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree $2k+1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ to a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree three on $\mathbb{R}^m$, where $m=\binom{n+k-1}{k}$, and preserves both GAS and Lyapunov stability. As a consequence, the problems of deciding whether the origin is GAS or Lyapunov stable for rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields of any degree, of any fixed odd degree $d \geq 3$, and of degree three are pairwise many-one equivalent. - In the second part we prove that there is a fixed dimension $n_*$ and a fixed odd degree $d_*$ such that the set of rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^{n_*}$ of degree $d_*$ whose origin is GAS is many-one complete. This is done by "transferring" many-one completeness between several different problems, starting from the solvability of a Diophantine equation and eventually arriving at our desired GAS decision problem.
item.dc:creator: Ivan O. Shevchenko, Jun Liu, Xinzhi Liu
